correctness.rationale: Complete trace comparison proves that all core vertices and at least one private path vertex per core are mandatory. Non-core traces have at most one core vertex, while every base trace has at least two, using H connected and h>=2. The only remaining collisions are between closed-twin base vertices both taking a leaf-only private state. The at-most-one-per-class criterion is necessary and sufficient; independent multiplication of the disjoint state contributions establishes the exact polynomial and its boundaries. Independent direct code testing verified 583744 subsets in 49 connected-core cases; finite evidence supplements, not replaces, the uniform proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Closed-neighborhood identifying codes are also called differentiating-dominating sets. The ordinary corona joins each base vertex to every vertex of an attached factor; a two-corona attaches a pendant two-edge path, producing different closed-neighborhood traces. The 2022 paper uses the correct two-corona but asserts only the identification number and selected constructions, not the all-cardinality twin-class enumerator.

originality.rationale: The exact identification number 2h, mandatory core vertices, and two explicit code constructions were already established for H◦2 by Foucaud–Lehtilä. The new claim is not that scalar result. Their inspected Proposition 9/Theorem 10 do not establish the complete three-state classification with one leaf-only choice per closed-twin class, an all-cardinality polynomial for arbitrary cores, its minimum-code multiplicity, or the determination of the twin-profile by roots. Canoy–Malacas address a distinct ordinary corona product. Targeted queries found no equivalent count; absolute priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and research-record searches are necessarily incomplete; unindexed or uninspected equivalent formulas may exist.
The 2022 source already implies minimum cardinality 2h and necessary selected vertices; the new claim is confined to exact sufficiency, counts, and twin-profile consequences.

value.rationale: The two-corona is a natural established extremal identifying-code family. Exact counts of every sensor-code size and every minimum code refine the previously known minimum without being implied by it. The normalized polynomial encodes the entire closed-twin partition of the core by its nonzero negative roots, with exact size support, minimum-code multiplicity and optional independent-sensor reliability. These are natural structural invariants and provide a complete labeled census for all connected core graphs, not arbitrary parameter slices.
